title: Electric potential and potential energy; Charged particles in uniform electric fields
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: F04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; F04-ap1#t1 term and clue written for the game; F04-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; F04-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: F04-1#N.5b, F04-ap1#N.2a, F05-1#N.3, F04-1#N.7b, F04-ap1#N.6, F05-1#N.5b, F04-1#N.13b, F05-1#N.8b, F05-1#N.15, F05-1#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Volt
items.clue: Name of the unit equal to 1 J C⁻¹.

items.label: Electric potential energy
items.clue: External work needed to assemble a set of charges from infinitely far apart.

items.label: Test charge
items.clue: Probe placed at P to sample V; its own size and sign do not affect the value.

items.label: Scalar
items.clue: Kind of quantity with a sign but no direction, so several values add as plain numbers.

questions.stem: An electron is released from rest at a location where the electric potential is 50 V. Moving under the electric force alone, it reaches a location where the electric potential is 250 V. How much kinetic energy has it gained? Use e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

Three particles, each with charge +q, are fixed on a straight line at x = −d, x = 0 and x = +d. A student claims that the system's total electric potential energy is kq²/(2d), reasoning that the middle particle's interactions with the two outer particles cancel. Which evaluation of the claim is best supported?

options.text: Correct: the forces on the middle particle cancel, so its two pair energies cancel.
Incorrect: each particle has its own share of each pair, so U_E is 5kq²/d.
Incorrect: U_E is a scalar, so all three pair energies add, giving 5kq²/(2d).
Incorrect: each pair's U_E depends on 1/r², so U_E is 9kq²/(4d²).

questions.stem: Two horizontal parallel plates, 2.5 cm apart in a vacuum, have a potential difference of 150 V between them. What is the magnitude of the acceleration of an electron between the plates? Gravity is negligible. Take e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg.

options.text: 1.1 × 10¹³ m s⁻²
2.6 × 10¹³ m s⁻²
6.6 × 10¹¹ m s⁻²
1.1 × 10¹⁵ m s⁻²

questions.stem: System X consists of two protons, and system Y consists of a proton and an electron. In each system an external force moves the two particles farther apart. For which system or systems does the electric potential energy increase?

options.text: Only for system Y, the proton and electron
Only for system X, the pair of protons
For both systems, as the particles separate
For neither system, since U_E falls as r grows

questions.stem: A proton and an electron are each released from rest beside one plate of a pair of oppositely charged parallel plates in vacuum: the proton beside the positive plate and the electron beside the negative plate. Each moves under the electric force alone to the opposite plate. Which particle arrives with the greater speed, and why?

options.text: Neither: charges of equal magnitude give them equal final speeds.
The electron: both gain equal kinetic energy, and its mass is smaller.
The proton: the electron moves to higher potential, raising its U_E.
The electron: its larger acceleration gives it more kinetic energy.

questions.stem: A proton (charge +e, mass m) and an alpha particle (charge +2e, mass 4m) each start from rest and are accelerated by the electric force alone through the same potential difference. What is the ratio of the alpha particle's final kinetic energy K_α to the proton's final kinetic energy K_p?

options.text: K_α/K_p = 1
K_α/K_p = 2
K_α/K_p = 4
K_α/K_p = ½

questions.stem: Particles with charges +Q and −Q are fixed a distance d apart. Point M is midway between them. Which statement about the electric potential at M is correct?

options.text: It is zero, although the electric field at M is not zero.
It is not zero, because the electric field at M is not zero.
It is 4kQ/d, twice the potential that +Q alone produces there.
It has no value until a test charge is placed at M.

questions.stem: A proton enters the uniform electric field between two oppositely charged, horizontal parallel plates, moving parallel to the plates. Gravitational effects are negligible. Which statement describes the proton's motion while it is between the plates?

options.text: It turns to follow a field line, then moves straight toward the negative plate.
It follows a parabolic path, with constant acceleration toward the negative plate.
It curves toward the negative plate with an acceleration that grows as it nears it.
It moves along a circular arc, since the force on it is perpendicular to its velocity.

questions.stem: In the worked example, the electron left the plates deflected sideways by a distance y. The potential difference across the plates is now doubled, and the electron enters at twice the speed. What is its sideways deflection at exit now?

options.text: y
2y

questions.explanation: y = ½at², with a ∝ |ΔV| (×2) and t = L/v (×½, so t² × ¼). The deflection is 2 × ¼ = ½ of y.

questions.stem: A proton and an alpha particle are placed, one at a time, at the same point in a uniform electric field. The alpha particle has twice the charge of the proton and about four times its mass. Gravity is negligible. What is the ratio (acceleration of the alpha particle) / (acceleration of the proton)?
questions.explanation: Correct. Acceleration = charge × E ÷ mass, so the ratio is (2/4) = 1/2. The alpha particle accelerates half as much.
